producer_report.summary: Athena now measures throughput and reviews it. (1) `athena status` has a throughput section computed from job records alone: landed jobs per UTC day; the median minutes per landed job over the newest 20 landed jobs, with a median for each of six stages (reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild); idle time between jobs (gaps between merged working spans, so overlapping jobs leave none); and minutes on jobs that did not land. (2) `Athena::throughput_review` runs from `review_passes` (drain start and sweeps). It is due every 10 landings after the previous review (the first 10 if none), or when the median is more than 20% worse than the previous review's and a job has landed since (`throughput_due`). When due, the verifier's model gets the section plus a copy of docs/design in a read-only workspace and names the biggest bottleneck, the architectural change and the expected minutes saved per landed job. (3) The top proposal is queued through `StewardRequest::new` as a design request titled "Throughput design: ...". Priority follows the prediction: at least 10 minutes urgent, at least 5 high, at least 2 normal, else low. Every review is recorded in a new `athena.throughput-review/1` record, which holds the baseline median, the prediction and the follow-ups. (4) A later review records a follow-up once for each earlier prediction whose cited change has landed. The change is a landed job, other than the design request, whose text cites the review id. The follow-up holds predicted saving, baseline median, measured median over at most 10 later jobs, and measured saving. A model failure still writes a no-proposal record so the cadence advances. Docs: hestia.md section 12 and a CHANGELOG entry. Tests added: 2 in status.rs, 6 in hestia.rs, 2 in records.rs. After my last edit I re-ran fmt, clippy and the one changed test. The full-suite pass came before that edit and had one failure, listed in open_issues.

Departure from plan decision 7: while a throughput design request is open, the review does not call the model at all. It writes a no-proposal record with a note, to save money. The plan had the model run and the request skipped.
Landing and rebuild is one measured tail (the last invocation's end to the landing outcome), because no record separates the rebuild.
The review uses Role::Steward and models.verifier, so no config change was needed. It runs from review_passes, so the model wait falls at the next drain start or sweep, not at the landing.
I did not re-run the full `cargo test --locked` after the final fix to job_plan.rs. Only that test was re-run.
Not done: the follow-up needs at least 1 landed job after the change (FOLLOWUP_MIN_JOBS=1), as planned, so a thin measurement is final once written.
mistakes: My first draft subtracted checks minutes from the landing tail, which was wrong because checks run before the verifier. I removed the subtraction before the first test run.
My first fixtures used a 'u' in job id suffixes and outcome totals that did not match the invocations. Tests caught both and I fixed them.
I ran the full suite once and it truncated its output, which cost a second run to find the one failing test.
learnings: A new request job's records must reconcile with the gate: an outcome's totals must equal the sum of the job's invocation records, so test fixtures must compute totals from their invocations.
Record and job ids need a 4-character lowercase Crockford base32 suffix, which excludes i, l, o and u.
`athena status` text is built only in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs. job_plan.rs guards against the word "plan" in an unplanned job's status.
Role::Steward invocations load into Records.steward_runs, not into any job.
Checks run before the verifier invocation, so they sit in a gap between invocations, outside any invocation's time.
`Iterator::sum` of f64 over an empty iterator gives -0.0, which prints as "-0.0"; use store::positive_zero.
The Bash tool here refuses grep, head, tail and wc; use the Grep and Read tools. `cargo test -q` keeps full-suite output small.
